_comment: Procedural table for Classes. Per procedural_generation_scope_proposal.md #5's authoring-burden note, classes are low-VOLUME (a world has a handful, not 20+) but high-DEPTH per unit -- so this table is shaped differently than items/enemies: a small set of fully fleshed archetype seeds (identity, resource, tier themes, evolution, whyItWorks) crossed with a shared, tier-slot-tagged ability template pool. {primaryLabel}/{secondaryLabel}/{majorSkill}/{minorSkill}/{resource} placeholders are filled by lib/proceduralGenerators.js from the world's own stat/skill labels (lib/worldFlavor.js) -- never hardcoded English. Ability level numbers (1/5/10/15/20, 25/30/35/42/48, 51/55/60/65/70/75, 80/85/90/95/99) follow prompts/classContentPrompt.js's own schema exactly, so a procedurally-generated class sheet renders identically in shape to an AI-generated one.

archetypes.coreResourceDescription: Builds as the Brawler takes and lands hits in melee; spent to fuel heavier follow-up strikes.
archetypes.visualShift: Scarring stops being hidden and starts being deliberate -- wrapped, painted, worn like a record.

tier1.title: Fists First
tier1.theme: Learns to turn punishment into momentum.

tier2.title: The Long Fight
tier2.theme: Starts outlasting opponents who hit harder but tire faster.

tier3.title: Unbroken
tier3.theme: Damage stops being a cost and starts being fuel.

tier4.title: The Last Stand
tier4.theme: Becomes hardest to kill exactly when it matters most.

archetypes.capstoneQuote: I stopped counting hits a long time ago. I just count who's still standing.
archetypes.tagline: Hit me. I've got more where that came from.
archetypes.evolutionCost: A season spent sparring somewhere unofficial, plus whatever scrap it takes to keep showing up.

whyItWorks.label: The {minorSkill} Synergy
whyItWorks.text: {resource} generation quietly rewards investing in {minorSkill}, not just raw {primaryLabel} -- a Brawler who ignores it caps out early.

whyItWorks.label: The {resource} Gate
whyItWorks.text: Every heavy ability spends {resource}, so a Brawler who avoids taking hits never gets to throw their best ones.

whyItWorks.label: The Fantasy Arc
whyItWorks.text: Level 1 — someone who wins fights by refusing to fall down. Level 50 — someone who's stopped falling down at all. Level 99 — someone the fight itself can't outlast.

archetypes.coreResourceDescription: Builds while staying at range and landing consecutive hits; spent to guarantee a shot connects or crits.
archetypes.visualShift: Movements slow down and simplify -- nothing wasted, nothing rushed, right up until the shot itself.

tier1.title: Line of Sight
tier1.theme: Learns that distance is a weapon in its own right.

tier2.title: Held Breath
tier2.theme: Starts trading mobility for accuracy on purpose.

tier3.title: The Steady Hand
tier3.theme: Every shot starts landing exactly where it was meant to.

tier4.title: One Shot, One Ending
tier4.theme: Becomes the reason a fight ends before it starts.

archetypes.capstoneQuote: Everyone else is still aiming. I already fired.
archetypes.tagline: Give me one clean line and this is already over.
archetypes.evolutionCost: A custom sight, hand-fitted, plus a debt owed to whoever fitted it.

whyItWorks.label: The {minorSkill} Synergy

whyItWorks.label: The {resource} Gate
whyItWorks.text: Guaranteed-hit abilities all spend {resource}, so a Marksman who keeps missing never earns the shots that matter.

whyItWorks.label: The Fantasy Arc
whyItWorks.text: Level 1 — someone who's just good with a gun. Level 50 — someone who doesn't miss. Level 99 — someone whose reputation ends fights before the trigger's pulled.

tier1.title: Jury-Rigged

tier2.title: Load-Bearing

tier3.title: The Architect
tier3.theme: Begins rewriting the rules of what a rigged system can do.

tier4.theme: Becomes the reason nothing on the battlefield behaves normally.

archetypes.capstoneQuote: You're fighting the room. I built the room.

tier2.title: Triage

tier4.title: Nobody Dies Today

archetypes.coreResourceDescription: Builds while staying calm and landing consecutive hits under pressure; spent to guarantee the next shot connects clean.
archetypes.visualShift: Everything about their stance simplifies -- no wasted motion, nothing about them reads as rattled anymore.

tier1.title: Line of Sight

tier2.title: Held Breath
tier2.theme: Starts trading movement for accuracy on purpose.

tier3.title: The Steady One
tier3.theme: Every shot starts landing exactly where it was meant to.

tier4.title: One Shot, One Ending
tier4.theme: Becomes the reason a confrontation ends before it escalates.

archetypes.capstoneQuote: Everyone else in this is panicking. I already took the shot.
archetypes.tagline: Give me one clean line and this is already over.
archetypes.evolutionCost: A shot taken under real pressure, that had to land, and did, verified by someone who was there for it.

archetypes.coreResourceDescription: Builds from reading a situation and exploiting weak points in real time; spent to trigger a bigger prepared advantage on demand.

tier1.title: Working the File
tier1.theme: Learns to make information do the fighting.

tier2.title: Cross-Reference
tier2.theme: Starts stacking small advantages into real combos.

tier3.title: The Whole Picture
tier3.theme: Begins seeing angles nobody else in the room has found yet.

tier4.title: Total Coverage
tier4.theme: Becomes the reason nothing in this situation stays hidden.

archetypes.capstoneQuote: You're working off what you can see. I'm working off everything.
archetypes.tagline: Give me thirty seconds with the file and this is already decided.
archetypes.evolutionCost: A read on a situation nobody else caught, that turned out to be exactly right, verified after the fact by people who doubted it.

archetypes.coreResourceDescription: Builds from stabilizing people under pressure and working fast; spent on interventions that shouldn't be possible on scene.
archetypes.visualShift: Their kit gets heavier and more personal -- every tool has a story about the call it was used on.

tier1.title: First On Scene
tier1.theme: Learns to keep people stable in the worst five minutes of their life.

tier2.title: Triage
tier2.theme: Starts making the calls nobody wants to make first.

tier3.title: The First On Scene
tier3.theme: Becomes the reason a crisis doesn't become a tragedy.

tier4.title: Nobody Dies On My Watch
tier4.theme: Becomes able to pull someone back from the actual brink.

archetypes.capstoneQuote: I've called it too many times. Not this one.
archetypes.tagline: Stay conscious. I'll handle the rest.
archetypes.evolutionCost: A call worked solo, outside protocol, that saved someone the book said couldn't be saved.

whyItWorks.label: The {minorSkill} Synergy

whyItWorks.label: The Fantasy Arc
whyItWorks.text: Level 1 — someone who stabilizes patients. Level 50 — someone who makes triage calls that save the scene. Level 99 — someone crisis itself starts deferring to.

archetypes.coreResourceDescription: Builds from staying unnoticed and working an angle before anyone clocks it; spent to guarantee a blown cover turns into a real edge.
archetypes.visualShift: Nothing about their presence draws a second look anymore -- not because they're hiding, just because they've stopped standing out.

tier1.title: Blend In
tier1.theme: Learns that most rooms can be worked without ever being noticed.

tier2.title: Working the Angle
tier2.theme: Starts turning timing and position into real advantage.

tier3.title: The Clean Exit
tier3.theme: Begins taking what's needed mid-operation, not just before.

tier4.title: No Trace Left
tier4.theme: Becomes able to turn any blown cover into a decisive edge.

archetypes.capstoneQuote: You'd be amazed what a room gives up, if nobody's watching you take it.
archetypes.tagline: I was never really here. Ask anyone.
archetypes.evolutionCost: An operation pulled clean with no exit plan going in, and a way out found anyway.

whyItWorks.label: The {minorSkill} Synergy

whyItWorks.label: The Fantasy Arc
whyItWorks.text: Level 1 — someone who's good at not being noticed. Level 50 — someone who turns any cover into an opening. Level 99 — someone no room actually clocks.

archetypes.coreResourceDescription: Builds from calling in connections and reading who owes who; spent to force a situation to bend the Fixer's way.
archetypes.visualShift: Their phone never seems to stop buzzing, and somehow, wherever they walk, someone already knows they're coming.

tier1.title: Know a Guy
tier1.theme: Learns that most problems already have someone who can solve them, for a price.

tier2.title: Working the List
tier2.theme: Starts turning favors into a real tactical resource.

tier3.title: The Only Call That Matters
tier3.theme: Begins bending a situation through connections alone.

tier4.title: Everybody Owes Somebody
tier4.theme: Becomes the reason a losing situation doesn't stay lost.

archetypes.capstoneQuote: I never had the muscle. I just always knew who did, and what they owed me.
archetypes.tagline: Give me one phone call and this problem gets a lot smaller.
archetypes.evolutionCost: A favor called in that cost more than it should have, from someone who had every right to say no, and didn't.

whyItWorks.label: The {minorSkill} Synergy
whyItWorks.text: {resource} builds faster with {minorSkill} invested, rewarding a Fixer who backs connections with real competence.

whyItWorks.label: The {resource} Gate
whyItWorks.text: The strongest favor plays spend {resource}, so a Fixer who never engages directly never has enough banked to turn a situation.

whyItWorks.label: The Fantasy Arc
whyItWorks.text: Level 1 — someone who knows people. Level 50 — someone whose connections turn a situation. Level 99 — someone half the city owes, one way or another.

archetypes.coreResourceDescription: Builds as the Cursed Knight lands and takes hits, the curse feeding on violence either way; spent to let it briefly take the wheel.
archetypes.visualShift: The curse stops staying hidden under armor and starts showing through -- cracked light, wrong angles, something underneath that isn't quite them anymore.

tier1.title: The First Crack
tier1.theme: Learns to use the curse without quite letting it use them.

tier2.title: Feeding the Thing
tier2.theme: Starts outlasting opponents by giving the curse just enough to stay quiet.

tier3.title: The Willingly Damned
tier3.theme: Damage stops being a cost and starts being what the curse was always for.

tier4.title: What's Left Underneath
tier4.theme: Becomes hardest to stop exactly when there's least of them left in control.

archetypes.capstoneQuote: I stopped fighting the curse a while ago. Now we just agree on who it's for.
archetypes.tagline: Hit me. It just gives the thing inside more to work with.
archetypes.evolutionCost: A night spent letting the curse fully surface, survived, with someone trustworthy standing by to pull them back if it went wrong.

whyItWorks.label: The {minorSkill} Synergy
whyItWorks.text: {resource} generation quietly rewards investing in {minorSkill}, not just raw {primaryLabel} -- a Cursed Knight who ignores it caps out early.

whyItWorks.label: The {resource} Gate
whyItWorks.text: Every heavy ability spends {resource}, so a Cursed Knight who suppresses the curse entirely never gets to unleash their best.

whyItWorks.label: The Fantasy Arc
whyItWorks.text: Level 1 — someone carrying a curse they mostly control. Level 50 — someone who's learned to use it on purpose. Level 99 — someone it's no longer clear is fully in control of the fight, including to them.

archetypes.coreResourceDescription: Builds the closer the Hunter gets to something that shouldn't exist; spent to turn that dread into a shot that lands exactly where it needs to.
archetypes.visualShift: Their eyes stop reacting to things that should make anyone flinch -- calm in exactly the moments calm shouldn't be possible.

tier1.title: Know the Signs
tier1.theme: Learns to read what's wrong about a place before it's too late to leave.

tier2.title: Steady Hands
tier2.theme: Starts turning fear into precision instead of hesitation.

tier3.title: The Unflinching
tier3.theme: Every shot starts landing exactly where it was meant to, no matter what's on the other end.

tier4.title: It Should Fear You Now
tier4.theme: Becomes the reason something ancient starts hesitating first.

archetypes.capstoneQuote: It's been the scariest thing in every room it's walked into. Not tonight.
archetypes.tagline: Give me one clean line, and it doesn't matter what you actually are.
archetypes.evolutionCost: A hunt finished alone against something that had already won every previous encounter, and didn't win this one.

whyItWorks.label: The {minorSkill} Synergy
whyItWorks.text: {resource} builds faster with {minorSkill} invested, rewarding a Hunter who studies the threat instead of just aiming at it.

whyItWorks.label: The {resource} Gate
whyItWorks.text: Guaranteed-hit shots all spend {resource}, so a Hunter who never confronts the dread head-on never earns the shot that matters.

whyItWorks.label: The Fantasy Arc
whyItWorks.text: Level 1 — someone who hunts what shouldn't exist. Level 50 — someone those things start avoiding. Level 99 — someone that's become the thing other hunters tell stories about.

archetypes.coreResourceDescription: Builds from performing minor rites and listening to things better left unheard; spent to channel something far larger, at a real cost.
archetypes.visualShift: Their notes stop looking like research and start looking like correspondence -- annotated by something that's been writing back.

tier1.title: Marginalia
tier1.theme: Learns that forbidden texts answer questions if you're willing to ask them the right way.

tier2.title: Layered Rites
tier2.theme: Starts stacking small workings into real, dangerous combinations.

tier3.title: The Well-Read
tier3.theme: Begins channeling rites the source material explicitly warned against.

tier4.title: It Answers Now
tier4.theme: Becomes the reason something on the other side starts listening back.

archetypes.capstoneQuote: Every text I've read told me not to go further. I stopped listening to that particular warning a while ago.
archetypes.tagline: Give me thirty seconds with the right rite and this fight is already decided.
archetypes.evolutionCost: A rite performed alone, at real cost, that the source material specifically said not to attempt without someone else present.

whyItWorks.label: The {minorSkill} Synergy
whyItWorks.text: {resource}-spending rites scale off {minorSkill} as much as {primaryLabel}, rewarding an Occultist who diversifies study rather than fixating on one text.

whyItWorks.label: The Fantasy Arc
whyItWorks.text: Level 1 — someone who's dabbled in things they shouldn't have. Level 50 — someone who's rewritten what those things can do for them. Level 99 — someone the things they study now actively answer to.

archetypes.coreResourceDescription: Builds from warding allies and holding a line against what's trying to get in; spent on interventions no ordinary rite could manage.
archetypes.visualShift: Symbols and wards start following wherever they stand, scratched, chalked, or simply felt -- a line nothing crosses without cost.

tier1.title: First Ward
tier1.theme: Learns that belief, applied correctly, protects as well as it comforts.

tier2.title: The Vigil
tier2.theme: Starts making the hard calls about who needs a ward first.

tier3.title: The Unpossessed
tier3.theme: Becomes the reason a losing fight doesn't become a possession.

tier4.title: Nothing Gets In
tier4.theme: Becomes able to pull someone back from further gone than faith should reach.

archetypes.capstoneQuote: I've lost people to worse things than this. Not tonight.
archetypes.tagline: Stay behind the line. I'll hold whatever's trying to get through it.
archetypes.evolutionCost: A vigil kept over someone possessed, alone, until whatever had them let go instead of the other way around.

whyItWorks.label: The {minorSkill} Synergy

archetypes.coreResourceDescription: Builds from moving through the spaces between what's real and what isn't; spent to guarantee a strike lands from somewhere it shouldn't.
archetypes.visualShift: Their outline stops being entirely reliable in low light -- not gone, just less certain than it should be.

tier1.title: Between Places
tier1.theme: Learns that most thresholds can be walked, not just crossed.

tier2.title: Working the Dark
tier2.theme: Starts turning shadow and silence into real advantage.

tier3.title: The Half-Gone
tier3.theme: Begins striking from places that shouldn't have an angle on the fight at all.

tier4.title: Nowhere Is Safe
tier4.theme: Becomes able to turn any shadow into a decisive edge.

archetypes.capstoneQuote: You'd be amazed what's on the other side of a shadow, if you're willing to actually walk into it.
archetypes.tagline: I was already behind you. I've been behind you for a while.
archetypes.evolutionCost: A crossing made alone into wherever the shadows actually lead, and a way back found before it closed.

whyItWorks.label: The {minorSkill} Synergy

whyItWorks.label: The {resource} Gate
whyItWorks.text: The best tricks all spend {resource}, so a Shadow-Walker who never opportunistically grabs an edge never gets to use them.

whyItWorks.label: The Fantasy Arc
whyItWorks.text: Level 1 — someone comfortable in the dark. Level 50 — someone who turns any shadow into an opening. Level 99 — someone no threshold actually keeps out.

archetypes.coreResourceDescription: Builds from commanding belief and breaking the will of things that shouldn't have will to break; spent to force a moment through sheer conviction.
archetypes.visualShift: The old regalia gets worn again, deliberately this time -- a symbol repurposed instead of buried.

tier1.title: The Old Voice
tier1.theme: Learns that command, once learned, doesn't actually go away.

tier2.title: Holding the Flock
tier2.theme: Starts turning old devotion into a real tactical resource, for better reasons this time.

tier3.title: The Reformed Prophet
tier3.theme: Begins bending the shape of a fight through belief alone, on purpose, for the first time.

tier4.title: What I Built, I Can Unbuild
tier4.theme: Becomes the reason something that shouldn't be reasoned with, listens anyway.

archetypes.capstoneQuote: I know exactly what this kind of voice can do. That's precisely why you should be worried it's pointed at you now.
archetypes.tagline: Follow me. I promise this time it actually ends well.
archetypes.evolutionCost: A congregation walked away from, and something worse talked down instead, using every old trick for a reason that finally justified it.

whyItWorks.label: The {minorSkill} Synergy
whyItWorks.text: {resource} builds faster with {minorSkill} invested, rewarding a Cult Leader who backs command with real competence, not just old habits.

whyItWorks.label: The Fantasy Arc

t1.name: First Contact
t1.effectTemplate: A quick opening strike that builds {resource}. Damage scales with {primaryLabel}.

t1.name: Read the Room
t1.effectTemplate: Passively grants bonus Accuracy on the first action each combat. Bonus scales with {secondaryLabel}.

t1.name: Steady Footing
t1.effectTemplate: Passively reduces the AP cost of movement by a small, flat amount.

t1.name: Quick Study
t1.effectTemplate: Spends a turn observing a target, revealing one weakness. Effectiveness scales with {majorSkill}.

t1.name: Bank It
t1.effectTemplate: Generates bonus {resource} whenever a turn ends without spending any. N/A — Binary Unlock.

melee.name: BREAK THE LINE
melee.effectTemplate: A committed charge that closes distance and staggers the target. Damage and stagger scale with {primaryLabel}.

ranged.name: DEAD CENTER
ranged.effectTemplate: A guaranteed-hit shot that spends all current {resource} for bonus damage. Damage scales with {resource} spent.

tech.name: TRIGGER EVERYTHING
tech.effectTemplate: Detonates every active rigged effect at once. Damage scales with number of effects active and {majorSkill}.

support.name: HOLD THE LINE
support.effectTemplate: Grants all allies a shield and cleanses one status each. Shield strength scales with {primaryLabel}.

stealth.name: TAKE THE OPENING
stealth.effectTemplate: An immediate free action against a target who hasn't acted yet this combat. Damage scales with {secondaryLabel}.

social.name: STAND WITH ME
social.effectTemplate: Rallies all allies, clearing Fear and granting bonus Accuracy for two turns. Bonus scales with {primaryLabel}.

t2.name: Momentum Shift
t2.effectTemplate: A follow-up action usable only after the opener connects. Damage scales with {majorSkill}.

t2.name: Hardened Nerve
t2.effectTemplate: Passively grants resistance to Fear and Panic-type effects.

t2.name: Second Wind
t2.effectTemplate: Spends {resource} to recover a moderate amount of health or Energy.

t2.name: Pressure Point
t2.effectTemplate: A precise strike that applies a stacking debuff. Stack potency scales with {secondaryLabel}.

t2.name: Efficient Motion
t2.effectTemplate: Passively reduces the AP cost of this class's core ability by 1.

t3.name: Ignore the Rules
t3.effectTemplate: Bypasses a portion of target's damage reduction or resistance. Ignored amount scales with {majorSkill}.

t3.name: Overcharged
t3.effectTemplate: Passively increases maximum {resource}, and abilities scale further past the old cap.

t3.name: No Wasted Motion
t3.effectTemplate: Chains directly into a second action without spending additional AP. Chain damage scales with {primaryLabel}.

t3.name: Turn the Tide
t3.effectTemplate: Converts a negative status on self into a matching positive effect. Duration scales with {secondaryLabel}.

t3.name: Unshakeable
t3.effectTemplate: Passively grants immunity to being staggered or interrupted while above half health.

t3.name: Exploit the Gap
t3.effectTemplate: Deals bonus damage against any target already affected by a status. Bonus scales with {majorSkill}.

melee.name: NOTHING LEFT STANDING
melee.effectTemplate: A sweeping strike hitting every adjacent enemy, spending all {resource} for bonus damage per target.

ranged.name: EVERY SHOT COUNTS
ranged.effectTemplate: Fires at every visible enemy simultaneously, each guaranteed to hit. Damage scales with {primaryLabel}.

tech.name: CASCADE FAILURE
tech.effectTemplate: Chains a rigged effect through every enemy in range, escalating with each jump. Scales with {majorSkill}.

support.name: NOT ON MY WATCH
support.effectTemplate: Fully restores one ally and grants them a full extra turn. Restoration scales with {primaryLabel}.

stealth.name: GHOST STEP
stealth.effectTemplate: Becomes untargetable for one turn and repositions freely. N/A — Binary Unlock, enables a follow-up next turn.

social.name: THE ROOM AGREES
social.effectTemplate: Forces every enemy in range to skip their next action. Duration scales with {primaryLabel}.

t4.name: Legend Precedes You
t4.effectTemplate: Passively grants bonus {resource} generation whenever an ally lands a killing blow nearby.

t4.name: Refuse to Fall
t4.effectTemplate: Once per combat, an attack that would drop this character to 0 health leaves them at 1 instead.

t4.name: Reap the Reward
t4.effectTemplate: Spends all current {resource} for a massive single-target strike. Damage scales with {resource} spent and {majorSkill}.

t4.name: Beyond Training
t4.effectTemplate: Passively grants a flat bonus to every scaling stat this class's abilities reference.

t4.name: Answer for Everything
t4.effectTemplate: Cleanses every negative status on self and grants a matching positive one. N/A — Binary Unlock.

melee.name: THE LAST STAND
melee.effectTemplate: While below quarter health, gains massive bonus damage and cannot be reduced below 1 health for three turns.

ranged.name: ONE SHOT, ONE ENDING
ranged.effectTemplate: A single guaranteed-crit shot that ends the encounter's biggest remaining threat outright below a health threshold.

tech.name: TOTAL OVERRIDE
tech.effectTemplate: Seizes control of every rigged effect and hostile system in range for one full turn.

support.name: NOBODY DIES TODAY
support.effectTemplate: Fully restores and shields every ally simultaneously, once per encounter.

stealth.name: NOTHING WASTED
stealth.effectTemplate: Converts every advantage gained this combat into one devastating, unavoidable strike.

social.name: NOBODY BREAKS FIRST
social.effectTemplate: Every ally becomes immune to Fear, Panic, and morale effects for the rest of the encounter, permanently.

designNotes.value: Rolled procedurally from a fixed archetype seed -- solid as a baseline kit, but a hand pass on ability names/flavor is recommended before this becomes a player's main.
Rolled procedurally -- the numbers and structure are sound, but this is the category where a manual polish pass earns the most per minute spent.
